text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The saga of Kisumu molasses plant takes a new twist as Opposition Member of Parliament Raila Odinga loses bid to block the official receiver from offering the plant to another bidder.
- Two people are hacked to death and a 10-year-old seriously injured when more than 100 raiders attack a camp inhabited by victims of 1992/93 ethnic violence in the Rift Valley.
- Nakuru Chief Magistrate William Tuiyot tells the Norwegian government to desist from commenting on the pending appeal by jailed political prisoner Koigi Wa Wamwere.
- The government discloses that any imported corned beef will be subjected to re-testing by the Kenya Bureau of Standards.
- Energy Minister Darius Mbela says Kenya does not necessarily need electricity it imports from Uganda as it is too little nad is only imported when available.
-The Coffee Board of Kenya is to charge a .082 of a U.S. dollar as a marketing levy for every kilogramme of coffee auctioned during the 1995/96 year.
- A syndicate of corrupt lawyers and legal officers at City Hall are plotting to defraud the cash-strapped council of 3.0 billion shillings owed to it by rate defaulters.
- Some opposition officials reject opposition Democratic Party chairman Mwai Kibaki and Kennedy Kiliku as the choice for sole opposition presidential candidate.
